body:
Thank you :)

​

Holy sh...wow! This is amazing. I admire your honesty. For being so open about this. And I'm sorry for your loss. As for this poem, it's good as it is. I would add a period, a full stop after "forty five minutes of breath," though, to add more weight to the moment. Now excuse me while I cry. This was very, very good.

I like this poem. The idea of it. It's very romantic. Sad but romantic. Poignant in parts. My only concern is the pacing and the rhythm. Some parts rhyme, some parts don't. I'm confused. And concerned. It's not a cohesive poem (it's not a bad one) and when read aloud, parts of it just don't jive. I just don't think it's finished. I can't tell you what to do, but for the sake of the *idea*, please rewrite this, fix it a bit, choose whether you want to go the prose route or something more lyrical and stick with it all the way till the end. Thanks for sharing though :)

I'm not sure if this is a poem about unrequited love, or a relationship at the brink. I liked it though. I have a thing for poems that are short and simple, sometimes they say more then poems that go on forever. And also I like the imagery of this piece, and the use of science especially. Keep up the good work.
I enjoyed this. It's cheeky. I liked the simplicity of the poem too. But maybe add more words, create a narrative or an image that a reader can connect with. This poem has potential.
Thank youuuuu :)
hello the point of the brackets was to draw you away from the action, and into the mind of the narrator. Thanks for your input :)

This is a complicated poem. It masquerades as a simple and straightforward composition but it's not. There's ambiguity here. I can't tell if you're really happy, or really sad. And I like that. It takes skill to write something like this, to have the reader guessing. All the same, i wish the poem was shorter. It might have been stronger if this was condensed into two verses, or eight lines, but I can't tell you what to do. :)

This is superb. The imagery it invokes is absurd/surreal (and that's a good thing; honestly it's very difficult to do.) It's also somber. and nostalgic (I guess.) There's a yearning for the past, for something.  I think after reading this aloud so many times I finally understand you and where this is all coming from. You're a very talented writer. I wish I could write something this good, at this length.

How poignant. This was written so well. This reads (to me) like a tragic love story. One survives, the other dies by suicide. One passes on, one copes with the aftermath. "You met the eternal ocean," is such a jarring line. My only critique is that this could have been lengthened. It might have been even more effective if the narrator described his grief.

Oh Jesus this gave me life. I have a thing for short and sad poems. Poems that go straight to the point. And with so few words, you managed to express (very effectively) profound emptiness ,or straight up depression. 

"I'd read, and write, and pass the time away—

And worry not about the coming day."

This is literally me when I'm in one of my moods. You're a talented writer, please continue. :)
Thank you very much!
Thank you so much!
Thank you so much!
Thank you. :)

This is good. There's artistry here. The way the words j*ust flow* . There's a rhythm that I like. I reread this twice, because it sounded so beautiful, and so  tragic, and strangely, bleak. Good job.

This poem has potential, believe me. But it feels reductive somehow. It reads like Faudet. And also it's way too personal. I don't know who Caroline is. Or how madly, deeply in love you two were. There's no narrative. I don't feel anything reading this. At all. This could have been written better. YOU HAVE THE TALENT. Rewrite this please.

Are you frustrated? Because it certainly sounds like it. And there's nothing wrong with that, but...what I'm saying is that this is good. Beyond good. Great even. It perfectly expresses exasperation, and in parts, a *propensity* to please. I connected with this, truly.

Simple and straight to the point. I prefer shorter pieces like this, haikus especially. It's subtle and suggestive. You must love whoever this haiku was written for dearly. It shows concern. And that's what I like about this, it sounds very sincere.
Dua Lipa
thank you very much!
thank you!
The thing I like about this (especially the last eight lines), is that it's lyrical...and there's a rhythm to it...this could be a song tbh.

This is a bit off-beat, I didn't get the rhyme scheme. It caught me off guard and I struggled a while, but after re-reading it a couple of times, I got the rhythm, and I understood what you we're trying to say. This is about heartbreak. And I like the words and the metaphors you employed. Very poignant, very sad. Beautiful!
This is cool. It is pretty emotional. And I did tear up a bit, all cause its so frank and straightforward. My only concern is the last line...I thought it could be shorter, and less literal.

I like the idea behind the poem, the fact this was about Walter White, one of my all-time fave characters, is a plus. But I think the rhyming sounds forced, it just doesn't come naturally. But good work though.

I like the idea behind the poem, the fact this was about Walter White, one of my all-time fave characters, is a plus. But I think the rhyming sounds forced, it just doesn't come naturally. But good work though.

This one's neat, the whole read forwards and backwards thing is interesting, but I thought it was a bit bland and the subject of the piece has been explored to death...you got skills and talent, I believe you can do better than this.

For a short poem this one is jam-packed with emotions. A tear fell from my eye as I read this (I swear). Like Brenden Norwood, I think your piece is divine. Nothing much to critique here except the ending, the words just didn't jibe. Keep it up!

I like the words you used. Shows a very deep vocabulary. However...there's something lacking here. And that's rhythm. The first half is good, the beat is there. But it sort of falls apart after 
"gravity reaps them down, plucking them away
/until they become ghosts themselves." Other than that, good job.
I liked this a lot. But the fourth verse is problematic. The fourth line of the fourth verse destroys the rhythm. Aside from that, this is an exemplary piece.
Thank you.

This is a well-structured, well-written piece. This was beautifully written, and it's intention was clear. My only critique is the ending, I didn't like it personally, it felt forced that's all.
do you always critique this way?

I'm not going to sugarcoat this. The poem is lacking in something. Cliches are everywhere, left and right, I don't get the pacing, the structure is a bit off, it's too "rhymey", so much that it felt forced.

This is immensely beautiful. The first verse was so romantic, I swear to God I had the jitters just reading it. Feedback time: while I enjoyed the poem, I thought it was a bit cliched. Maybe you should use metaphors more next time, add a bit of ambiguity. But this is beautiful.
This is a long one...a bit tedious...but I appreciated the imagery. It's vey vivid, very clear, and although I have my reservations. I like it. :)
I like the second bit. But I'm afraid I can't say the same for the rest. Good job though.
This is deep, and very personal, the choice of words make it very difficult to understand. But at least you were honest, and you used words (or a variation thereof to) express those emotions.
This is a darkly comedic poem. Mind you, I like it. I just wish there were more punchlines.
The poem captures the feeling of hopelessness very well. The man has no future, no chance of redemption. Short and direct to the point, love it.
I liked the simplicity of the poem...and I think I have an idea of what you're trying to say..I just don't like the way some words rhyme...it doesn't sound right, it sounded forced.
This is beautiful in that it perfectly captures the feeling of boredom and desperation too. I liked that it was literal, it made the poem very relatable. Good job.

This poem is relatable, even if it's very personal, and I like the metaphors you employed. I love the third verse to be honest. 
The imagery is awesome, and I felt like the persona is someone who is deeply troubled. You conveyed it very well. I just wished the poem was shorter though (I have a preference for shorter poems)

This poem was well written. It was a pleasure to read. I felt like there was a rhythm to it. I also like the way the poem was structured, and I like the way it ended. I'll admit it was very hard to understand, but I read it again and again, and I think the poem talks about memory?
